articles.title: Tyreek Hill reunion takes an unexpected turn as Chiefs reportedly prepare to work out former wide receiver
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs’ interest in Tyreek Hill has hit a new complication, with the team reportedly preparing to bring former wide receiver Justin Watson
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs’ interest in Tyreek Hill has hit a new complication, with the team reportedly preparing to bring former wide receiver Justin Watson in for a visit. Kansas City had been linked with Hill as it looks to strengthen its receiving group, but the five-time All-Pro’s recovery from a serious knee injury and a potential NFL suspension make his return less straightforward. Watson offers a different option. He knows the Chiefs’ offense, has won two Super Bowls with the team and could provide depth without the same level of uncertainty. The visit does not guarantee a deal, but it gives Kansas City another route to consider.Chiefs reportedly prepare to bring back Justin WatsonPer many reports, the Chiefs are expected to host Watson at their facility on Monday, following a report from team reporter Pete Sweeney. Sweeney wrote, “Watson is expected to be in town on Monday.”The visit could include a workout, although that has not been confirmed. Kansas City has not announced a signing, so Watson’s return remains a possibility rather than a done deal.Watson spent three seasons with the Chiefs from 2022 through 2024, helping the team win two Super Bowls. He also played for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before joining Kansas City, giving him valuable NFL experience. At 30, he is unlikely to offer the same explosive upside as Hill, but his familiarity with the offense could make him a practical addition.The Chiefs have reasons to look for help. Rashee Rice remains a key part of the receiving group, while Xavier Worthy, Jalen Royals and rookie Cyrus Allen are among the other options. Worthy has delivered mixed results this season, and Tyquan Thornton’s ankle injury has added another concern.Watson could help fill the gap left by Thornton, particularly as a receiver who has experience stretching the field. He ran a 4.44-second 40-yard dash at his 2018 pro day, a sign of the speed that once made him an appealing option.If Kansas City signs him, Watson could begin on the practice squad and earn opportunities on game days. A place on the active roster is also possible, depending on his performance and the team’s needs.Why Tyreek Hill’s potential Chiefs reunion still uncertainHill’s return would bring a much bigger name and a different level of excitement. He helped Kansas City win Super Bowl LIV and built a strong connection with quarterback Patrick Mahomes before the Chiefs traded him to Miami in 2022. His speed and ability to turn short passes into big gains made him a major part of the offense.The Athletic’s Mike Silver previously reported that Kansas City could have a “strong interest” in bringing Hill back. However, Hill’s recovery from a serious knee injury is not the only concern.Heavy reported that Hill’s recent civil trial included his admission that he verbally threatened and pushed his ex-wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro Hill. The NFL is also investigating a potential violation of its personal conduct policy, which could result in a suspension. Those issues leave his availability uncertain even if he regains enough fitness to play.That makes Watson a useful alternative to consider, though not a direct replacement for Hill’s impact. Watson offers familiarity and experience, while Hill could provide greater big-play potential if he returns to form and is cleared to play.Kansas City does not have to choose between the two immediately. A visit with Watson would allow the team to assess one option while it continues to evaluate Hill’s situation.For now, Watson’s reported visit is the more concrete development. articles.title: Josh Allen decide el thriller de los Bills ante los Rams en la NFL
articles.standfirst: Los Buffalo Bills ganaron 34-37 a Los Angeles Rams en el SoFi Stadium
articles.summary: Los Buffalo Bills ganaron 34-37 a Los Angeles Rams en el SoFi Stadium
articles.body: Josh Allen ganó la primera prórroga de su carrera, tras siete derrotas, al liderar el triunfo por 37-34 de los Buffalo Bills ante Los Angeles Rams en el SoFi Stadium, donde Greg Rousseau bloqueó un intento de gol de campo de Harrison Mevis que pudo decidir el encuentro para los angelinos. Allen completó doce de sus diecinueve pases para 210 yardas y un 'touchdown', con una intercepción, y fue devastador por tierra, con 121 yardas y otra anotación en diez carreras. Su potencia volvió a resultar decisiva en la posesión que culminó con el gol de campo ganador de Tyler Bass desde 45 yardas. James Cook aportó 111 yardas y dos 'touchdowns' a la carrera, pero también cometió dos 'fumbles', uno de ellos perdido en la prórroga. Khalil Shakir encabezó las recepciones de Buffalo con 80 yardas en tres capturas, seguido por Ty Johnson, con 72. Los Bills mejoraron su balance a 4-1 pese a recibir trece penalizaciones, más de diez por tercer partido consecutivo. Los Rams, que quedaron con un balance de 2-3, tuvieron a Matthew Stafford como motor ofensivo, con cuarenta pases completados de 54 para 383 yardas y tres 'touchdowns', sin intercepciones. Puka Nacua acumuló diecisiete recepciones para 138 yardas y una anotación, mientras que Davante Adams recibió dos pases de 'touchdown' y Kyren Williams sumó 49 yardas y un tanto por tierra. El encuentro llegó al último cuarto con una ventaja de 19-14 para Buffalo y se convirtió en un intercambio de golpes. Nacua adelantó a los Rams, Allen respondió por tierra y Adams volvió a igualar. Cook pareció encarrilar el triunfo visitante con una carrera de cinco yardas para el 34-27, a 1:39 del final. Stafford evitó la derrota al conducir una serie de ocho jugadas y 63 yardas, culminada por Williams a cinco segundos del cierre. En la prórroga, una recepción de 57 yardas de Shakir puso a Buffalo en posición de anotar, pero Cook perdió el balón y los Rams recuperaron la posesión. Rousseau mantuvo con vida a los Bills al bloquear el intento de Mevis. Allen aprovechó la segunda oportunidad, volvió a castigar por tierra y dirigió una serie de 35 yardas que permitió a Bass sellar el triunfo a 1:55 del final de la prórroga.

articles.title: NFL Madrid Games: así se traslada el ‘hospitality made in USA’ al Bernabéu
articles.standfirst: El partido del 8 de noviembre entre Cincinnati Bengals y Atlanta Falcons cuenta con hasta ocho propuestas de hospitalidad distintas
articles.summary: El partido del 8 de noviembre entre Cincinnati Bengals y Atlanta Falcons cuenta con hasta ocho propuestas de hospitalidad distintas
articles.body: La industria del deporte y el entretenimiento tiene muchas fechas marcadas en rojo en el calendario, y una de ellas es el 8 de noviembre de 2026. El NFL Madrid Game vuelve al Bernabéu tras el sold out del año pasado, y en él se volverá a poner a prueba la capacidad de la competición de fútbol americano para trasladar el hospitality made in USA al mercado español. Entre los cerca de 80.000 espectadores que puede albergar el estadio del Real Madrid C.F. habrá miles de aficionados al deporte, pero también otros miles que ven en este evento una herramienta para reforzar relaciones con clientes, socios e invitados, lejos de la formalidad de una sala de reuniones. El fútbol americano lo facilita, con un formato competitivo en el que las fases y las pausas durante el partido dejan un espacio natural para la conversación, mientras que la gastronomía, las actividades previas y las actuaciones musicales amplían la experiencia más allá del encuentro. Si bien el evento deportivo es el reclamo y el producto en torno al que gira la propuesta de valor, para muchos es el tiempo compartido con sus invitados lo que realmente importa. Ahora bien, el crecimiento del segmento b2b ha obligado al sector a diversificar su oferta y dejar atrás la idea del VIP como un producto monolítico. Propiedades deportivas y promotores musicales han ido ampliando el abanico de opciones de hospitalidad, creando puertas de entrada por la franja baja de precios, dando forma a productos de mayor exclusividad y adaptando algunos paquetes a los objetivos comerciales. Lejos de vender el mejor asiento, el hospitality tiene el desafío de conseguir que el partido tenga los alicientes necesarios para alcanzar el objetivo comercial de quien compra. En menos de tres años, los clubes de LALIGA han añadido más de 15.000 nuevas localidades de hospitality para adaptarse a este nuevo escenario, elevando el peso de este segmento de público del 3% al 4,5% del aforo total de los estadios. Y hay margen de recorrido, pues el porcentaje reservado para este tipo de entradas en otras ligas roza incluso el 8%. Su aparición también se ha hecho notar en los ingresos, llevando a la mayoría de clubes a alcanzar ingresos récord por matchday y a ampliar de forma importante sus clubes de empresa. El Bernabéu llega a esta cita con una de las ofertas premium más completas de Europa tras su remodelación, y sobre todo con el haber de una primera edición en la que superó el examen de recrear el made in USA en España. Los Paquetes Hospitality del NFL Madrid Game 2026 -pueden adquirirse a través de Ticketmaster, partner global de la NFL- se reparten por distintos espacios del estadio. Desde los restaurantes Arzábal Bernabéu, Sur, Puerta 57, Plaza Mahou hasta las localidades de primer anfiteatro en las tribunas norte y sur, pasando por los salones vinculados al museo del club, como el Museum Lounge y el Museum History Lounge o el Trophy Lounge. Son formatos que combinan las mejores ubicaciones con vistas al terreno de juego con gastronomía y servicio de atención personal. Una empresa que quiere estrechar la relación con un cliente no necesita necesariamente el mismo espacio que otra que busca ampliar su red de contactos o premiar a su equipo de trabajo. Disponer de distintos grados de privacidad, ambientes y servicios permite ajustar la propuesta al tamaño del grupo, al perfil de los invitados y, sobre todo, al objetivo de quien los reúne. Para los grandes recintos, la oportunidad está en convertir esa variedad en una herramienta comercial recurrente. En la Premier League, el Arsenal FC es un buen ejemplo de esa evolución. Su plataforma de hospitality permite filtrar por tipo de evento —fútbol masculino, femenino o conciertos— y por formato de experiencia, con categorías como dining, exclusive lounges, experiential, informal o private box. La lógica no parte sólo del asiento, sino de la necesidad del cliente: comer, relacionarse, vivir una experiencia más inmersiva o disponer de un espacio privado. La música avanza en la misma dirección. La serie de conciertos de Shakira en Madrid, con más de 600.000 espectadores en 12 conciertos, incorpora experiencias VIP con acceso preferente, espacios de hospitality, oferta gastronómica y entretenimiento previo. La propuesta también diferencia entre formatos más abiertos, terrazas elevadas y suites privadas para grupos reducidos, con servicio personalizado y pases de parking incluidos. Ese salto es relevante porque amplía el mercado potencial. El hospitality tradicional solía asociarse a un palco, una buena localidad y catering. El nuevo modelo se parece más a una a una oferta más amplia y segmentada: distintos niveles de privacidad, relación, acceso, comodidad y contenido para distintos perfiles de comprador. El fomento de este tipo de paquetes de hospitalidad son clave en la generación de ingresos directos para los promotores de eventos, pero también para elevar el impacto económico que dejan en el territorio a través de un turismo internacional y de mayor poder adquisitivo. El 2025 NFL Madrid Game dejó más de 70 millones de euros en el territorio, y el sector hotelero registró uno de los mejores fines de semana del año con un 90% de ocupación en zonas como Centro, Chamartín y Chamberí. En total, fueron más de 42.000 visitantes internacionales. Por su parte, la restauración alcanzó un volumen económico cifrado en hasta 21,2 millones de euros, impulsado por un gasto medio diario del visitante internacional de entre 50 euros y 100 euros.

articles.title: "He takes care care of his body....": Travis Kelce receives major boost as Chiefs veteran weighs in on his future
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has given the Kansas City Chiefs another reason to believe they can make a deep playoff run.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has given the Kansas City Chiefs another reason to believe they can make a deep playoff run. At 37, the veteran tight end continues to deliver on the field, even after considering retirement during the offseason. Now, new teammate Kenneth Walker has shared his thoughts on Kelce’s future, and his assessment could interest Chiefs fans hoping to see the tight end stay in the NFL beyond this season. Walker has watched Kelce work behind the scenes since joining Kansas City and believes the veteran still has plenty to offer. His comments also highlight the work that goes into maintaining a long career.Kenneth Walker believes Travis Kelce can play for several more yearsKelce entered the 2026 season with questions surrounding his future. After a difficult 6-11 campaign for Kansas City last year, he chose to return for another season, signing a three-year deal with the franchise.His decision has paid off so far. The Chiefs opened the season 4-0, with Kelce playing a key role in their passing game. Through the opening four games, he recorded 16 receptions for 246 yards and two touchdowns, leading Kansas City in both catches and receiving yards.Walker, who joined the Chiefs after spending the first four seasons of his career with the Seattle Seahawks, has seen firsthand how Kelce prepares for games. The running back believes the tight end's commitment to his physical condition could help him extend his career.“Yeah, definitely,” said Walker on if Kelce can play another few years. “I feel like that goes to show how he takes care care of his body as well. I even seen him in the off season the way he was working in the training room and making sure his body was good before practices and everything. He’s playing at a high level too.”Walker's observations offer a glimpse into the work that fans rarely see. Kelce's experience and preparation remain important assets as the Chiefs pursue another championship.Kenneth Walker praises Travis Kelce and Patrick MahomesWalker has made an immediate impact in Kansas City himself. Entering Week 5, he led the NFL with 537 rushing yards and was on pace for a potential 2,000-yard season. His strong start has added another dimension to the Chiefs' offense.Despite his individual success, Walker stressed the importance of having experienced players such as Kelce and Patrick Mahomes around him.“They know what it takes to win, and they’re both two great competitors,” said Walker. “We’re going to need them this season.”Mahomes has also started strongly after recovering from an ACL injury, recording nine touchdown passes and two interceptions for a 106.2 passer rating.Walker said both veterans made him feel welcome after his arrival and helped him understand the team's culture.“Yeah, a big impact, honestly,” said Walker. “When I first got here, they welcomed me with open arms and just seeing what type of people they are off the field, they always want to help in the community and everything. They want to be together as a team, and I feel like that creates that bond that you need to be able to be successful and go to where you want to be at the end of the season.”With crucial games against the Los Angeles Chargers, Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos approaching after their bye week, the Chiefs will need contributions from across the roster. Kelce's experience, Mahomes' leadership and Walker's production could prove vital as Kansas City looks to maintain its unbeaten start.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cowboys DC Christian Parker moving from sideline to coaches' booth, says Jerry Jones
articles.summary: The Cowboys' defense is 31st in the NFL in yards allowed per game.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker is set to be moved from the sidelines to the coaches' booth for the rest of the season, owner and general manager Jerry Jones told 105.3 The Fan on Tuesday .

"You search for what we can do differently that would give us better results," Jones said on his 84th birthday . "That's the main emphasis that we would spend some, let's say, specific attention to areas. We're going to coach the defense from not on the field, but up above. Parker's going up above.

"You should be looking for ways to adjust and make changes to improve. That's the point of improving from the results we had the last few weeks."

The Cowboys dropped to 2-3 on the season following Thursday's loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Parker, who was hired in January , has already seen criticism directed his way from the likes of Wink Martindale and Mike Tomlin . Through five weeks the Dallas defense is 31st in the NFL with 395.4 yards allowed per game and has allowed a league-worst 168.4 rushing yards per game.

Thursday's defeat also marked the 12th straight game dating back to last season that Dallas has allowed at least 20 points.

Parker has held himself accountable publicly for the defense's lapses, but in an attempt to provide further assistance the Cowboys are bringing in longtime NFL defensive coordinator Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant .

Parker and Pettine worked together previously when the two were with the Green Bay Packers in 2019.

Jones made sure to say these decisions are not to say that Parker is overwhelmed by the responsibilities, but are a way to help find answers on the defensive side of the ball.

This is the second straight season the Cowboys will move their defensive coordinator from the field to the coaches' booth. Matt Eberflus made the move last season heading into Week 15 .

Eberflus, like Parker, was in his first year in the role. At the time, the Cowboys ranked 31st in points allowed, were giving up 30 points per game, and were 29th in yards allowed per game at 374.9 yards. They ended up losing two out those final three games, allowing an average of 30 points per game.

The Cowboys fired Eberflus following the season.

articles.title: NFL reverses course, says Zxavian Harris is eligible to sign with team after trying to play for LSU
articles.summary: Zxavian Harris was ultimately left off LSU's roster after trying to return to college.
articles.body:
The NFL is shifting gears on defensive tackle Zxavian Harris. After initially ruling Harris would not be eligible to sign with a professional team this season, the NFL reversed course Monday, telling teams Harris is an eligible free agent.

The league reportedly sent a memo to all 32 teams announcing that news, per NFL Network.

Harris and tight end Dae'Quan Wright found themselves the subject of controversy in September, when both men attempted to join Lane Kiffin at LSU despite spending time with NFL teams over the summer.

After going undrafted in the 2026 NFL Draft, Harris signed a deal with the New Orleans Saints. He was waived by the team in August, however. Wright spent time with the Philadelphia Eagles and Cleveland Browns before he was waived in late August.

With their NFL futures in jeopardy, Harris and Wright decided to see if they were eligible for a fifth year of college so they could play for LSU. That kicked off multiple contentious back-and-forths between Harris, Wright, LSU, the SEC and the NCAA.

In the end, LSU decided it wasn't worth risking the ire of the SEC and left both Harris and Wright off its roster.

The NFL then issued its initial ruling on both players , deeming them ineligible to sign with NFL teams in 2026 after attempting to return to college football.

Harris, however, had that decision reversed Monday after the NFL determined he did not participate in a single practice or game with LSU. Because of that, the league decided to make Harris an eligible free agent. Wright was not mentioned in the league's memo and remains ineligible to sign with an NFL team.

Now that he's eligible, it's unclear whether Harris will be signed by any team. Prior to his attempt to return to college, Harris was clearly on teams' radars, but was not good enough to make a final 53-man roster. Because of that, it's possible Harris draws attention as a possible practice squad player.

articles.summary: El Milano P1 de Premier Padel introduce un nuevo concepto para los trofeos de campeón
articles.body: El Milano P1 de Premier Padel, que se celebra del 19 al 25 de octubre, trae consigo una novedad importante en su edición de 2026: entregará a los campeones y campeonas anillos, como si de la NBA y la NFL se tratase. De la mano de Lagati Padel Jewels se han creado los Champions Rings, unos anillos engastados con diamantes, rubíes y esmeraldas que forman una imagen del Duomo sobre el fondo de la bandera tricolor italiana. "Para componer el Duomo en el centro del anillo, utilizamos 48 diamantes de tres tamaños diferentes, mientras que la bandera tricolor que lo rodea se realizó con ocho diamantes y otros tantos rubíes y esmeraldas", explica Angela Lagati, propietaria de la empresa. La espectacular joya incorpora también un pequeño detalle técnico de gran ingenio. "En el interior del anillo hemos colocado dos aletas ajustables con forma de pala de pádel. Sirven para adaptar la talla de la joya a dedos de tamaños muy distintos, pero también son un pequeño elemento simbólico que introduce el pádel en la propia estructura del anillo". Una iniciativa espectacular que da un toque distintivo a un torneo de los más especiales del calendario de Premier Padel y que se suma a una larga tradición de las ligas norteamericanas.

articles.body: Another exciting week of NFL action is in the books, capped off with Monday night’s back-and-forth thriller for the ages between the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams. Josh Allen and the Bills walked away with a 37-34 victory in overtime for the first OT victory of Allen’s career, while Sean McVay & Co. now sit at 2-3 after entering the year as Super Bowl favorites. Gaffes on special teams defined the Rams’ stunning loss, which should have been headlined by a historic night for MVP Matthew Stafford, who became the first quarterback in NFL history to throw for 150 touchdowns with two different teams. Rams kicker Harrison Mevin’s days with the team may be numbered after that loss, missing two field goals, including what should have been the game winner in overtime, blocked by Bills edge rusher Greg Rousseau.There are several players that could return to action next week worthy of monitoring. Bears quarterback Caleb Williams appears on track to make a potential return from a hamstring injury in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons. It remains to be seen if the Falcons will have their own starting quarterback, however, after Michael Penix Jr. suffered a rib injury on "Sunday Night Football." One player will also look to make his debut in a new uniform this week, after Texans head coach Demeco Ryans confirmed with reporters that the team traded for WR Marvin Harrison Jr. in a deal with the Arizona Cardinals. The former first-round pick now gets a fresh start with his college quarterback, C.J. Stroud, as he looks to rekindle his spark on offense.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more coming out of Week 5.

articles.title: Travis Kelce’s 87 & Running Foundation quietly makes another move for Operation Breakthrough’s Ignition Lab students amid financial controversy
articles.summary: Travis Kelce’s commitment to Kansas City youth continues to attract attention as his 87 & Running Foundation remains subject to financial controversy.
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s commitment to Kansas City youth continues to attract attention as his 87 & Running Foundation remains subject to financial controversy. As perThe Arizona Republic, the foundation’s IRS filings show that out of $1.5 million raised, nearly $470,000 went toward management and general expenses rather than charitable work.As per CharityWatch, the foundation reported raising approx. $1.5 million and spending roughly $1.1 million over a multi-year period, with about 41 cents of every dollar directed to charitable programs.A substantial share of spending was classified as general and management expenses, including payments to A&A Management, Kelce’s longtime business managers, Aaron and Andre Eanes’ company.Travis Kelce’s foundation reaffirms commitment to Ignition Lab studentsTravis Kelce may have taken a personal break from posting through the 87 & Running Foundation’s official Instagram account owing to the January 2026 financial scrutiny, his July 2026 marriage, new NFL season preparation, and other business commitments.But he brought his community work charm back by reinforcing a relationship built around opportunity, education, and support.In a heartfelt gesture highlighted by Operation Breakthrough, the NFL megastar brought a bucketload of kindness to students connected to the organization’s Ignition Lab program.Travis Kelce’s heartwarming kindness reaches Ignition Lab studentsOperation Breakthrough is a Kansas City nonprofit that provides children and families with education, opportunities, and essential support. The organization shared Travis Kelce’s heartwarming gesture in an Instagram post with the caption, “A whole lot of kindness delivered with love.”The post celebrated an act of generosity that brought attention to the students it serves and to the Kansas City Chiefs tight end who was behind the act.The nonprofit organization expressed gratitude toward the Kansas City Chiefs star for the thoughtful contribution of clothes of varied sizes to its Ignition Lab students.Two of its students stood by a stall with clothes of “large” size. If there was a “large” size clothing, then there could have been “medium,” “small,” and “extra-large” sizes too.The best part about the post was that it was a collaboration with Kelce’s 87 & Running Foundation. The foundation had not posted since January 2026, back when the financial controversy was doing cyberspace rounds.The social media post surely raises questions about the foundation’s financial details, especially if we come to think of it: where did the money for the clothes come from? Maybe from the billionaire pop singer’s husband’s pockets itself.Nevertheless, it highlights the personal side of the partnership and the significance of small gestures that make several young people feel valued and loved.The latest contribution also speaks volumes about Kelce’s relationship with Operation Breakthrough’s Ignition Lab program, particularly because it’s been central to his charitable work for years.Operation Breakthrough supports Kansas City childrenOver 700 urban Kansas City children come to Operation Breakthrough each weekday for nutritious food, lively learning, health and dental care, therapy, and TLC [Tender Loving Care].The kids’ parents work or attend school. The children’s ages range from infants to 14 years. About 20% of them are homeless. Over 70% of the families live on annual earnings lower than $12,000.About 65% of Operation Breakthrough’s children witness violence by the age of 5. Over 90% of the nonprofit’s 5-year-olds become “school ready” every year, compared to less than 50% of children affected by poverty nationally.Travis Kelce shares a special bond with Operation Breakthrough kidsTravis Kelce’s 87 & Running Foundation powers Operation Breakthrough’s Ignition Lab. The children at the Operation Breakthrough nonprofit use the word “my” when they talk about the Kansas City Chiefs star.For instance, “my favorite player…,” “my guy on the Chiefs…,” and “my friend Travis…” That is the level of bonding that the kids feel with the NFL megastar after having met him for years.“The Operation Breakthrough kids won me over the first time I walked in the building. The little ones loved to hear stories. The bigger kids tried to teach me to dance. They heard that I hadn’t had the time to buy a Christmas tree, so they gave me one they made with LED lights and plastic cups.You could just see how excited they are about learning, connecting - life. If these kids could light up my life with a Christmas tree they made out of disposable cups, just imagine what they can do when we band together to open their Ignition Lab,” Kelce said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Who does Josh Allen think is the ‘greatest thrower’ in NFL history after Bills-Rams overtime thriller
articles.summary: Josh Allen walked out of SoFi Stadium with his first career overtime win Monday night.
articles.body: Josh Allen walked out of SoFi Stadium with his first career overtime win Monday night. Matthew Stafford walked out with perhaps the strongest compliment one quarterback can give another.After the Buffalo Bills beat the Los Angeles Rams 37-34 on Oct. 12, Allen told ESPN that Stafford belongs in the conversation for the greatest pure thrower in NFL history. That praise came after Stafford threw for 383 yards and three touchdowns in the loss.Why does Josh Allen believe Matthew Stafford may be the greatest thrower in NFL history?HITC's Brogan Clasper highlighted Allen's comments on Oct. 13 after a game in which the two quarterbacks won in very different ways.Allen completed 12 of 19 passes for 210 yards and one touchdown. He did much of his damage with his legs, rushing for 121 yards and another score. Stafford leaned heavily on his arm and finished with nearly 400 passing yards.Allen came away impressed.“I’ve got an unbelievable amount of respect for Matthew [Stafford]. The way he plays the game, the way he’s always played it, he’s as tough as they come. I think if he’s not the greatest thrower of the football of all time, I don’t know who is. He spins it. He’s a competitor. He’s a guy that every quarterback just strives to be like,” Allen told ESPN after the game.That distinction matters. Allen did not call Stafford the greatest quarterback in NFL history. He specifically praised Stafford as a thrower of the football, which puts the focus on arm talent, ball placement and the ability to make difficult throws.The timing made the compliment even more interesting.Stafford entered Monday after an uneven opening stretch. He had thrown six touchdowns and six interceptions through the Rams' first four games, according to HITC. Against Buffalo, however, the 38-year-old looked far closer to the version Allen was describing.Stafford still lost the game.Buffalo survived 37-34 after Tyler Bass made a 45-yard field goal in overtime. Allen accounted for 331 total yards and two touchdowns while leading a Bills offense that found another way to win.The victory also ended a strange streak for Allen. He entered the night 0-7 in overtime games.“It’s the first OT that I’ve got, so this feels good being on this side [of a win],” Allen said afterward, according to PEOPLE.For Allen to spend part of that moment praising the quarterback he had just beaten says plenty about what he thought of Stafford's performance.How did Hailee Steinfeld’s rare appearance fit into Josh Allen’s first career overtime win?Allen also had his family watching from inside SoFi Stadium.PEOPLE reported on Oct. 13 that Hailee Steinfeld attended the game and watched from a suite as Buffalo completed the overtime win. Steinfeld, 29, and Allen, 30, married in May 2025 and welcomed their daughter, Harper, in April.Steinfeld typically attends Allen's games without drawing much attention from television cameras, according to PEOPLE. articles.title: 1 Trade to Put NFL's Best Teams Over the Top After Week 5
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL trade deadline is now less than a month away, but there is still plenty of time for Super Bowl hopefuls to address their most glaring weaknesses.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is now less than a month away, but there is still plenty of time for Super Bowl hopefuls to address their most glaring weaknesses.

The first five weeks of the 2026 season have provided plenty of evidence regarding which teams have the talent to make a deep playoff run and which still need an outside addition to reach their full potential. Whether it's through acquiring another pass rusher, upgrading a struggling secondary or getting their quarterback some help, a key trade could be the difference between lifting the Lombardi Trophy and suffering a painful postseason exit.

Many of the trades that would push certain teams over the top aren't exactly headline-grabbers. Because of how talented these rosters already are, an overlooked defender or experienced offensive lineman might be all it takes to unlock a lineup's true potential. There are certain situations, however, where a team would benefit from taking a bigger swing. These needle-moving stars may cost more, but they would help their new employer keep pace with the league's elite.

With that in mind, here is one trade each of the NFL's top teams—defined as having at least four wins through the first five weeks of the 2026 season—should consider after Week 5.

Baltimore Ravens receive: EDGE Josh Uche

Miami Dolphins receive: 2027 sixth-round draft pick

The Baltimore Ravens have weathered a storm of injuries to emerge as the frontrunner in a tough AFC North race. While the team is 4-1 and boasts one of the NFL's best offenses, some defensive upgrades are still needed for this club to be considered a true Lombardi Trophy contender.

Getting after opposing quarterbacks has been a challenge for Baltimore in 2026. The team has created pressure on a middling 20.2 percent of plays and has a pedestrian sack rate of 5.52 percent. With 10 sacks in five games, the Ravens are barely on pace to surpass the lowly 30 sacks they recorded during the 2025 campaign.

These numbers figure to improve when Baltimore gets top edge rusher Trey Hendrickson back from injury, but bringing in a crafty veteran like Josh Uche could help push this pass-rushing unit over the top.

Uche is languishing on an 0-5 Miami Dolphins team that has no hope of reaching the playoffs in 2026. While he's recorded a decent 20 tackles and a sack on the year, an uninspiring supporting cast is preventing him from making too much of an impact. A move to Charm City could be exactly what the seven-year veteran needs to return to the high level of play he displayed earlier in his career.

With Uche on an affordable one-year, $1.4 million deal, the Ravens could do far worse than rolling the dice on him becoming a solid piece of their edge rushing rotation. Parting with a late-round pick to bolster the defensive front with a player who recorded 11.5 sacks as recently as the 2022 season is worth the risk.

Philadelphia Eagles receive: 2027 seventh-round draft pick

After allowing an average of 280.4 passing yards per game and giving up 13 total passing touchdowns this season, the Buffalo Bills' championship hopes may hinge on whether their bottom-five ranked pass and scoring defense can become more reliable. This makes Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Kelee Ringo an intriguing trade target for the club.

Despite a strong 4-1 start, Buffalo has largely lacked consistency on the perimeter. Maxwell Hairston in particular has been a liability in coverage—notably allowing 44 yards and four key catches on seven targets to the New England Patriots in Week 4—and didn't draw a start in Week 5 despite head coach Joe Brady declaring the 2025 first-rounder would be in the lineup.

Hairston ultimately played just 17 defensive snaps against the Los Angeles Rams (a 20.7 percent snap share that was well below the 80-plus percent he had logged over the first month of the season) and still found a way to make several costly mistakes when he was on the field.

It's become readily apparent that the Bills can't rely on the sophomore defensive back to play a key role for their defense. Adding a big, physical corner like Ringo would provide an upgrade on the outside, one capable of matching up with the hulking wideouts Buffalo figures to come up against often during a Super Bowl run.

Ringo, a fourth-round selection in the 2023 draft, should be available after falling out of favor in Philadelphia. He was on the field for a career-high 28 percent of defensive snaps during the 2025 season, but has only contributed on special teams during the first five games of the 2026 campaign.

With Ringo playing out the final year of his rookie deal and unlikely to stick around the City of Brotherly Love beyond this trying season, dealing him outside of the NFC for a late-round pick would be a shrewd move for a reeling Eagles side that is falling out of contention. The 6'2", 207-pound corner could benefit from a change of scenery and would get every opportunity to reach his ceiling in a Buffalo secondary that has become downright desperate for capable defenders.

Jacksonville Jaguars receive: DT Moro Ojomo

Philadelphia Eagles receive: 2027 third-round draft pick, 2027 seventh-round draft pick

The Jacksonville Jaguars have displayed few weaknesses during their 4-1 start, but there is still room for one of the NFL's top defenses to further improve. Moro Ojomo's presence could elevate this group to No. 1.

With the team relying heavily on veteran Arik Armstead to produce at a high level, the potential for the interior pass rush to become a point of failure is high. Bringing in Moro Ojomo would give Armstead some support and provide an insurance option in case the 32-year-old defensive tackle gets injured or declines.

Ojomo has steadily developed into one of the league's more promising young defensive linemen. The 2023 seventh-rounder worked his way up the depth chart and became a key piece in the defensive trenches last year, posting a career-best 38 tackles and six sacks.

Although Ojomo has yet to record a sack in 2026, he's still putting consistent pressure on the quarterback while playing approximately two-thirds of Philadelphia's defensive snaps . He's on the final season of his rookie deal and is set to cash in with a sizable contract when he hits free agency in the spring.

Philadelphia's asking price may be steep, but Ojomo would be worth the investment as a player who fits in both the near- and long-term plans for a Jacksonville franchise with Super Bowl aspirations.

Ojomo only recently turned 25 years old and still hasn't hit his ceiling. He's already developed from a raw prospect into a stable contributor and could still burst out as one of the NFL's top defensive tackles in the next few years. Sending over a Day 2 draft pick to an Eagles team trending towards a rebuild would allow the Jags to benefit from Ojomo's current contributions and position themselves to realize his upside with a long-term extension.

Kansas City Chiefs: Bring in Edge Khalil Mack

Kansas City Chiefs receive: EDGE Khalil Mack

Los Angeles Chargers receive: 2027 fifth-round draft pick

The Kansas City Chiefs' defense has flashed the sort of dominance it displayed regularly during the team's dynastical run, but an inability to consistently get after the opposing quarterbacks is a concern. Khalil Mack could be the player the Chiefs need to dial in their pass rush.

Kansas City is coming off a Week 5 bye undefeated, but the team is tied with the winless Miami Dolphins for the fewest sacks in the NFL with a meager four. While their pressure rate of 24.2 percent falls just outside the top-10, a league-worst 2.65 sack percentage indicates another proven finisher is needed along the defensive front.

There are few players in league history capable of providing the sort of disruption Mack brings to the table.

Although he's in the twilight of his career, Mack is still a nightmare for opposing passers to deal with. Across the first five games of 2026, the 35-year-old has recorded 10 pressures, five hurries, five QB hits and three sacks. The nine-time Pro Bowler is on pace for his best season since 2023 and still looks to have plenty of tread left on his tires.

Although the Chiefs don't have much financial wiggle room to make blockbuster trades, Mack is surprisingly affordable. He's on a one-year, $18 million contract that included a $10 million signing bonus, which means he would only be owed a shade over $6 million if he were dealt at this point in the campaign. That one-year deal, coupled with the Los Angeles Chargers' 0-5 start, makes an intra-AFC West trade more realistic.

While Mack is one of the more decorated defenders of the modern era, he's yet to win a ring during his 13-year NFL career. Joining forces with the Chiefs would give him a chance to do so, as his presence shores up Kansas City's most glaring weakness and gives the club a far better chance of raising another banner.

Minnesota Vikings receive: OG Ben Bredeson, 2027 seventh-round draft pick

Tampa Bay Buccaneers receive: 2027 fifth-round draft pick

The Minnesota Vikings are one of the surprise stories of the 2026 NFL season, jumping out to an unblemished 5-0 start. The team's hopes of staying perfect took a hit following the loss of starting left guard Donovan Jackson—who is done for the year after tearing his meniscus—and outside help may be required to patch that hole in the offensive trenches.

The team has given Joe Huber the first crack at replacing Jackson, but the undrafted sophomore has been shaky since entering the lineup. Per Pro Football Focus , Huber has already allowed three pressures, one QB hit and been flagged for two penalties across his 142 offensive snaps.

If Huber can't sort things out, Minnesota's brass should reach out to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to see if Ben Bredeson is available. The steady veteran is the type of reliable o-lineman who the Vikings could acquire and immediately slot into their starting lineup. He'd also get a chance to play alongside his brother, rookie Max Bredeson, who works as a fullback and special teamer in the Twin Cities.

The elder Bredeson offers plenty of starting experience stemming from his time with three different clubs. He entered the league as a fourth-round pick by the Baltimore Ravens in the 2020 draft and went on to start 58 games for the New York Giants and Tampa Bay Buccaneers over the past six years.

While the 28-year-old isn't likely to develop into a Pro Bowl-caliber talent, he's a natural replacement for Jackson who could help keep Minnesota's offense clicking. Bredeson in the midst of a three-year, $22 million contract that runs through the 2027 campaign, meaning he could provide both immediate assistance and continue to help the Vikings next season if he pans out.

San Francisco 49ers receive: WR Brian Thomas Jr.

Jacksonville Jaguars receive: 2027 second-round draft pick

The San Francisco 49ers have battled through a myriad of injuries to emerge as one of the season's top Super Bowl contenders, but the attrition their receiving corps has suffered will likely require a trade for someone like Brian Thomas Jr. to fix.

San Francisco wideouts appear to be cursed in 2026. Deebo Samuel became the latest to pick up an injury designation after straining his hamstring in a thrilling 32-29 win over the rival Seattle Seahawks. With Samuel reportedly set to be sidelined for several weeks, the team has to consider swinging blockbuster deal to stay afloat.

Following Marvin Harrison Jr.'s trade to the Houston Texans, Brian Thomas Jr. becomes the next promising but disappointing 2024 first-round wideout for teams to target. BTJ had an outstanding rookie campaign—earning a Pro Bowl nod after racking up 1,282 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns on 87 catches—but has regressed significantly over the past two seasons.

Considering the Jacksonville Jaguars are finding immense success despite phasing out the third-year wideout (who has just 105 receiving yards and one touchdown on nine catches across five games this season), it's possible Thomas could be had for the right price leading up to the trade deadline.

The Niners would likely need to give up a similar package to the 2027 second- and sixth-round picks that Houston sent the Arizona Cardinals for Harrison and a seventh-rounder, but that cost could be worth it for a young wideout with so much potential.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan's innovative offensive scheming has helped rehabilitate the careers of several other veteran cast-offs, a group Thomas could join if he lands in San Francisco. Thomas' rookie performance showed he has a superstar ceiling and, at the age of just 24, there is still plenty of time for him to get back on track.

Considering Thomas fits both the immediate and long-term plans of an organization looking to finally win a Super Bowl under Shanahan, surrendering a Day 2 pick is a worthwhile investment. If BTJ hits the ground running in San Francisco, the 49ers not only gain an immediate difference-maker capable of fueling a playoff run, but also secure their future No. 1 wide receiver in the process.

articles.title: Is Christian Parker already in trouble? Jerry Jones says Cowboys DC isn’t ‘overwhelmed’ as Mike Pettine arrives
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys are changing how Christian Parker runs their defense.
articles.body: The Dallas Cowboys are changing how Christian Parker runs their defense. Jerry Jones insists that does not mean the 32-year-old coordinator is in over his head.Parker will move from the sideline to the coaching box, while Dallas has hired former NFL head coach Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant. The changes come with the Cowboys sitting at 2-3 and ranking near the bottom of the NFL in several major defensive categories.Why are the Cowboys moving Christian Parker to the coaching box after five games?Jones confirmed the move Tuesday during his weekly appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas. ESPN's Todd Archer also reported that Parker will call the defense from upstairs rather than the sideline.The timing makes the decision impossible to separate from Dallas' defensive results.Through five games, the Cowboys rank 31st in total defense at 395.4 yards allowed per game. They are also allowing 27.2 points per game, placing them near the bottom of the league in scoring defense.Their run defense has been even more vulnerable. Dallas has allowed an NFL-high 168.4 rushing yards per game and 5.1 yards per carry, according to figures cited by ClutchPoints.Jones did not try to sell those numbers as acceptable.“I'm obviously disappointed in the results so far,” Jones said Tuesday, according to Field Level Media.He did, however, push back on the idea that Parker has become overwhelmed in his first season as an NFL defensive coordinator.Moving upstairs gives Parker a different view of opposing formations and personnel. It is also not unprecedented in Dallas. Archer noted that former Cowboys defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus made the same move last season when the defense struggled.What makes this change more significant is what Dallas did alongside it.The Cowboys did not simply change Parker's location on game day. They also added Pettine, a veteran defensive coach with experience as a coordinator for the New York Jets, Buffalo Bills and Green Bay Packers. Pettine also served as head coach of the Cleveland Browns.That naturally raises another question about how much help Dallas believes Parker now needs.What does Mike Pettine’s arrival mean for Christian Parker and the Cowboys defense?The Cowboys are publicly presenting Pettine as support for Parker, not his replacement.There is also existing familiarity between the two coaches. Parker worked under Pettine as a defensive quality control coach with Green Bay in 2019 and 2020. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer also worked on the same New York Jets staff as Pettine.Jones said those relationships played a role in the hire.“You put that all together and you've got some work to do to putting that all in place relative to the challenges you have when you really get into the ballgames,” Jones told 105.3 The Fan.Schottenheimer also believes Pettine can contribute immediately.“Coming into the situation where he will be very comfortable and can help very quickly,” Schottenheimer said, according to Field Level Media.Pettine most recently worked in a support role under Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores. Minnesota is 5-0 and leads the NFL with 16 sacks, while also using the league's highest blitz rate.Dallas now gets Pettine before a particularly relevant matchup.The Cowboys travel to Green Bay for a Sunday night game against the Packers. Pettine previously served as Green Bay's defensive coordinator and coached current Cowboys defenders Kenny Clark and Rashan Gary during his time there.None of that means Parker has been replaced or formally demoted. Jones has explicitly defended him, and Parker remains the defensive coordinator.But Dallas is also not standing still after five games of poor defensive production. Parker is changing locations, Pettine is joining the staff and Jones has openly acknowledged his disappointment.The Cowboys may not be calling it a crisis. articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns are going to Hollywood once again.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns are going to Hollywood once again.

On Tuesday, Hulu announced that Dan Fogelman's The Land will debut on Monday, Feb. 15, at 12 a.m. ET, just hours after the Super Bowl. The scripted family drama is centered around the Browns and features an ensemble cast that includes Christopher Meloni, Mandy Moore, Chace Crawford, William H. Macy and Omar Epps.

The Land follows the 2014 film Draft Day in featuring the Browns in a fictional setting.

Per Emily Longeretta of Variety , the show's synopsis states, "After several disappointing seasons, Cleveland Browns' head coach Danny Roarke (Meloni) has one last chance to turn around his football team. His fate rests on a newly drafted Ohio State quarterback — who just happens to be his son. Meanwhile, the owner, Hal Durkin (Macy), must decide which of his two daughters is best equipped to take over the team. 'The Land' is the story of two families, in which the high-stakes drama plays out not only on the field but also in the front offices of this NFL franchise, as a loyal fanbase wants a winning season now … or face big changes if they don't."

This marks Fogelman's second foray into the sports world, as he created the Fox drama Pitch , which told the story of the first female pitcher in MLB. Despite being canceled after one season, the series received critical acclaim.

The Browns are off to a 3-2 start this season, and they will remain in the spotlight after the Super Bowl when The Land officially drops on Hulu.

articles.title: New Justin Herbert Trade Rumors Reveal Chargers' Stance on QB Ahead of 2026 NFL Deadline
articles.summary: The idea of trading Justin Herbert is reportedly a "non-starter" for the Los Angeles Chargers ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.
articles.body:
The idea of trading Justin Herbert is reportedly a "non-starter" for the Los Angeles Chargers ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported he talked with a "high-level league executive" who said it would be "really interesting" if Los Angeles decided to trade Herbert for three first-round picks following its 0-5 start to the season.

Schefter took that idea to someone with the Chargers just to hear their thoughts and reported, "the person basically cut me off mid-sentence, stopped me in my tracks, and said, 'let me be very clear about this. We have never even discussed that idea. The sentence should we trade Justin Herbert has never once been uttered in our organization, nor will it be.'"

While the stance couldn't have been clearer, it's not difficult to see why the executive thought there was some merit to exploring a trade.

After all, Los Angeles has not won a single playoff game since selecting Herbert with the No. 6 overall pick of the 2020 NFL draft. There is no doubting his talent when he is playing at his best, but the evidence suggests the team is far away from being in a position to accomplish its goals even with him under center.

Trading Herbert for three first-round picks and adding those to their own draft capital would give the Chargers plenty of assets to accelerate a rebuild that is much-needed based on the start of the 2026 campaign.

The offensive line has been a problem , the defense is 22nd in the league in points allowed per game and no wide receiver has more than one touchdown catch through five games.

Los Angeles has a number of holes to fill throughout its roster, and the best way to do that for the long-term future is by finding success in multiple drafts spread out over different years. And having additional and valuable picks would increase the front office's chances at landing elite talent in those drafts.

Trading Herbert, Khalil Mack or other veterans could help the AFC West team stockpile a number of picks as it accepts the need to rebuild after such a disappointing start to the 2026 campaign.

However, it seems like the Chargers have no interest in trading Herbert as their franchise quarterback even as the losses pile up this season.

articles.title: Ja'Marr Chase's Fine for 'People's Elbow' Celebration Inspired by The Rock Rescinded After Appeal
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase was successful in his appeal of $29,852 in fines he received from the NFL.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase was successful in his appeal of $29,852 in fines he received from the NFL.

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the appeals officer found that the league was "assuming the worst of [Chase] and his teammate without discussing with the NFLPA" when it levied the punishment.

Chase asserted he was mimicking WWE legend The Rock and his "People's Elbow" finisher during a 20-6 win over the Houston Texans in Week 2:

Following his acrobatic touchdown grab in the second quarter, Chase placed his left hand under his right elbow and extended his right arm. Tee Higgins later did the same thing to celebrate one of his catches:

The league fined both wideouts for what it deemed an "offensive" gesture, which was used multiple times during the first two weeks. The Athletic's Jonathan Jones wrote it could "be interpreted as resembling a phallus."

Higgins offered his side to Kay Adams. He said he's a fan of WWE and The Rock. He and Chase were putting a different spin on one of the wrestler's signature moves:

This is just the most recent case of the NFL coming down hard on a player's celebration and having to walk back a fine on appeal.

Higgins told Adams he and Chase were putting the "People's Elbow" on ice and were "back in the lab" to think up a new celebratory taunt. After Chase's appeal was successful, maybe they can bring their ode to The Rock back.

articles.title: 'Thiccer Kicker' Harrison Mevis Released by Rams After 2 Missed FGs vs. Bills, NFL Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams are releasing kicker Harrison Mevis and signing Blake Grupe off the New York Jets' practice squad, per Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo of NFL Network.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams are releasing kicker Harrison Mevis and signing Blake Grupe off the New York Jets' practice squad, per Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo of NFL Network.

The 5'11", 243-pound Mevis, nicknamed "The Thiccer Kicker," missed two field goals in his team's 37-34 overtime home loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday evening. He pulled a 50-yard attempt wide left in the first quarter, and Bills linebacker Gregory Rousseau blocked Mevis' game-winning 48-yard attempt in overtime.

Mevis was 5-of-9 on field goals this season, including 3-of-6 from 40-49 yards. He made all 14 of his extra point attempts.

The 24-year-old made his NFL debut with the Rams on Nov. 9, 2025 after L.A. benched kicker Joshua Karty.

The Rams ran into special teams issues last year. Of note, their regular-season game against the Philadelphia Eagles ended in Philly blocking a game-winning field goal and returning it for a Jordan Davis touchdown in a 33-26 victory.

Karty missed five of 15 field goal attempts and three of 26 extra points. The Rams eventually waived him. Per head coach Sean McVay to reporters , L.A. wanted to keep two kickers but ultimately ran into a "roster management" issue.

The Rams also waived their long snapper, Alex Ward, on Nov. 10.

Mevis did very well for L.A. last year, making 18-of-19 field goals (including playoffs) and all 23 extra points.

However, this year featured a tough start, and McVay was not happy with the kicking game.

"In the kicking game, especially with our PAT, field goal, not even close to good enough," McVay told reporters . "It cost us the game tonight."

McVay had reason to be upset with special teams overall, as L.A. also allowed Bills running back Ray Davis to return the opening kickoff 70 yards (Buffalo ended that ensuing drive with a field goal).

Now the Rams are moving to a former Jet (Mevis played with New York during the 2025 preseason before being waived) for the second straight year.

Grupe kicked for the New Orleans Saints and Indianapolis Colts from 2023-2025. He had made 86-of-105 field goals (81.9 percent) and 96-of-98 extra points. He is 19-of-27 from 50-plus with a long of 60 yards.

The 5'7", 156-pound Grupe signed a one-year deal with the Colts last March but got waived on August 30. The Jets claimed him off waivers the next day.

Now he gets a great chance with the 2-3 Rams, whose talent is certainly better than their record shows. They'll look to move to .500 on Sunday when they host the Arizona Cardinals.

The Rams also waived their long snapper, Alex Ward, on Nov. 10.

Mevis did very well for L.A. last year, making 18-of-19 field goals (including playoffs) and all 23 extra points.

However, this year featured a tough start, and McVay was not happy with the kicking game.

"In the kicking game, especially with our PAT, field goal, not even close to good enough," McVay told reporters . "It cost us the game tonight."

McVay had reason to be upset with special teams overall, as L.A. also allowed Bills running back Ray Davis to return the opening kickoff 70 yards (Buffalo ended that ensuing drive with a field goal).

Now the Rams are moving to a former Jet (Mevis played with New York during the 2025 preseason before being waived) for the second straight year.

Grupe kicked for the New Orleans Saints and Indianapolis Colts from 2023-2025. He had made 86-of-105 field goals (81.9 percent) and 96-of-98 extra points. He is 19-of-27 from 50-plus with a long of 60 yards.

The 5'7", 156-pound Grupe signed a one-year deal with the Colts last March but got waived on August 30. The Jets claimed him off waivers the next day.

Now he gets a great chance with the 2-3 Rams, whose talent is certainly better than their record shows. They'll look to move to .500 on Sunday when they host the Arizona Cardinals.

articles.title: 49ers Trade Target Predicted by NFL Insider amid Latest Rumors on Deebo Samuel Injury
articles.summary: There could be a reunion in store before the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline.
articles.body:
There could be a reunion in store before the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline.

"I would say a name I've been wondering about is Jauan Jennings," NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said during a Tuesday appearance on The Pat McAfee Show . "… I expect his name to heat up a little bit over the next, probably couple days and weeks. And, obviously, the 49ers lost Deebo [Samuel] for a couple weeks too, so they make sense. That would be a name for me to keep an eye on."

Jennings has largely been a nonfactor for the Minnesota Vikings this season and enjoyed far more success during the last five seasons for the 49ers.

Wide receiver is also something of a concern for San Francisco, as Rapoport reported Samuel suffered a "bad" hamstring pull and could be reevaluated following the team's Week 8 bye.

Minnesota signed Jennings this offseason, but he has just two catches for nine yards and zero touchdowns through the first five games.

His lack of production also hasn't stopped the Vikings from winning, as they are 5-0 to start the campaign. Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson are the main weapons in the aerial attack, and the NFC North team also brought in Odell Beckham Jr. for veteran depth.

Perhaps a return to San Francisco could help Jennings rediscover his form.

After all, he posted a career-high nine touchdown catches just last year for the 49ers after finishing the 2024 campaign with career-high marks in receptions (77), targets (113) and receiving yards (975).

There is already chemistry in place with quarterback Brock Purdy, and it surely wouldn't take him long to get adjusted following a trade.

Here is a look at the financial situation as well:

With Samuel sidelined, Mike Evans is the only wide receiver on the 49ers with more than 84 receiving yards on the season. While tight end George Kittle and running back Christian McCaffrey are factors in the passing game, the NFC West team still needs more reliable options out wide for the immediate future.

Jennings would be a relatively low-cost addition with plenty of advantages from his experience with the team.

articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Jerry Jeudy Reveal Browns' Asking Price for WR Ahead of Deadline
articles.summary: While the Cleveland Browns are in the early AFC playoff picture thanks to a 3-2 start, they are reportedly interested in trading one of their veteran wide receivers in Jerry Jeudy.
articles.body:
While the Cleveland Browns are in the early AFC playoff picture thanks to a 3-2 start, they are reportedly interested in trading one of their veteran wide receivers in Jerry Jeudy.

"It's pretty well known around the league that Jeudy's available," NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported Tuesday (1:23 mark). "But my understanding is Cleveland would like something in that early third to fourth range. I'm just not sure they'll be able to get it. Bottom line, Jerry Jeudy's available. And he's another name I'd keep an eye on as we get closer to the deadline."

A third-round pick may just be too expensive for Jeudy at this point of his career.

While the Alabama product was a Pro Bowler during his first season with the Browns in 2024 with 90 catches for 1,229 yards and four touchdowns, he has seen a consistent drop in production since.

He finished the 2025 campaign with 50 catches for 602 yards and two touchdowns and has just eight catches for 81 yards and zero touchdowns through five games this season.

It should be pointed out that six of those eight catches have come in the previous two games, but Jeudy is still more of an afterthought in Cleveland's aerial attack.

Denzel Boston, Harold Fannin Jr. and KC Concepcion are all long-term building blocks for the AFC North team, while even Isaiah Bond has more receiving yards than Jeudy, with 86. That makes the latter expendable ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline.

But other teams around the league know he is expendable, which takes away some of Cleveland's leverage in any discussions.

The Browns may want a mid-round pick, but they might have to settle for less if they are actually going to trade him.

articles.title: Cowboys Defense Had 'Heart to Heart' Meeting After Loss to Bucs, DeMarvion Overshown Says
articles.summary: After a 2-3 start to the season, the Dallas Cowboys are searching for answers on defense.
articles.body:
After a 2-3 start to the season, the Dallas Cowboys are searching for answers on defense.

According to linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, the team had a "heart to heart" following Thursday's loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

"Looking ourselves in the mirror," Overshown said of what was discussed in the meeting, per Tommy Yarrish of the team's website. "Putting what we wanted our standard to be, we put that on the board. We went by bullet point, bullet point. Are we holding up to this? Are we being this? As a unit, how can we get closer? What is it? Just hearing from all of us. It really wasn't like a fire drill conversation, it was more so, 'What can I do to help you? What do I expect from you on Sundays, or every Monday walk throughs?' We've got to talk to each other like that because the ship is only going to go as far as the weakest person on the boat. As long as we all in this together, I think we're going to be great. I know we're going to be there."

The Cowboys spent the offseason trying to upgrade the defense, drafting Caleb Downs 11th overall and adding players like defensive tackle Quinnen Williams. Earlier this month, they traded for Pittsburgh Steelers star cornerback Joey Porter Jr.

But the results haven't shown up yet. Dallas has allowed the second-most total yards per game in the NFL this season (395.4) and the eighth-most points per game (27.2).

Despite the still-struggling defense, Overshown believes the Cowboys have the tools necessary to be one of the top units in the NFL.

"It's no reason why we couldn't be a defense that only allowed 10 points a game," Overshown said. "Our thing is not shooting ourselves in the foot, the mental errors. Once we get past that, we're going to be one of the best defenses in the league, we've just got to stop shooting ourselves in the foot."

Perhaps it is a matter of just putting things together, but the Cowboys' defense has looked lost through the first five games of the season.

articles.title: Bears' Montez Sweat Suspended After Violating NFL's PED Policy, Latest on Pro Bowler's Eligibility
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears will be without one of their pass rushers for the next two games.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears will be without one of their pass rushers for the next two games.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter, Montez Sweat has been suspended for two games without pay after violating the NFL's Performance-Enhancing Substances Policy.

Through five games, Sweat has logged five tackles and a pair of sacks, the third-most on the team. The 2023 Pro Bowler is coming off a season that saw him record 53 tackles and a career-high 10 sacks.

Sweat starts on the left side for Chicago, meaning Austin Booker will likely take over that role for the time being.

The good news is that Booker, a fifth-round pick in 2024, is putting together a career season so far, recording 14 tackles, four sacks and two forced fumbles. He's already surpassed his career high in forced fumbles and is just half a sack away from matching his career high in that category.

While losing Sweat is a tough break for the Bears, it will give Booker the chance to get an increase in reps.

Unfortunately for Chicago, right defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo is questionable heading into Sunday's matchup with the Atlanta Falcons because of a quad injury, so the team could be without another pass rusher.

Sweat will miss Sunday's game in Atlanta and a Thursday night matchup with the New England Patriots in Week 7. He'll be reinstated after that game, which will put him back on the field for a tough matchup against the defending champion Seattle Seahawks.

The Bears are coming off arguably their worst performance of the year in a 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers.

Injuries have been the story for the Bears early in the season, as they've been without quarterback Caleb Williams since Week 2. Williams has a chance to return to action this week, but is still questionable heading into Sunday.

articles.title: Steelers TE Jokes About 'Ass Chewings' from Aaron Rodgers, Details QB's Relationship with McCarthy
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth joked about getting called out by quarterback Aaron Rodgers across their two seasons as teammates.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth joked about getting called out by quarterback Aaron Rodgers across their two seasons as teammates.

"I've been on a couple ends of the ass chewings from Aaron, it's definitely not fun," Freiermuth said during a Tuesday appearance on the Pat McAfee Show (0:26 mark). "Definitely don't recommend it for anyone that comes into Pittsburgh. But it's all out of love, it's all because he wants the best for you. He sees something on the defense that he thinks he can exploit and if you're the guy that he asks to call on that situation, he expects you to be there on time. It's definitely tough to get on that same page as him but once you do, the sky's the limit."

Freiermuth also discussed Rodgers' dynamic with Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy.

"There's a different relationship between him and coach McCarthy," Freiermuth said (1:05 mark). "They've been together for so many years, so we don't really bat an eye. They have their little relationship that they like to have and do all that, so we just kind of keep it pushing."

Rodgers and McCarthy had multiple heated exchanges during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 4.

They're in the midst of their first year together in Pittsburgh, although they previously spent over 12 seasons together on the Green Bay Packers from 2006-18.

Rodgers earned two MVP awards during their shared tenure in Green Bay, while the Packers won a Super Bowl title in their 2010 campaign.

This season, the Steelers own a 3-2 record through five weeks.

Freiermuth has remained a consistent piece of Pittsburgh's passing attack, hauling in 19 receptions for 169 yards and four touchdowns across five appearances.

He's coming off a strong performance during the Steelers' 34-22 win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, catching five passes for 44 yards and two scores.

articles.title: Eagles' Big Dom DiSandro Vows to 'Get this Fixed' amid 3-Game Losing Streak
articles.summary: Dom DiSandro, the Philadelphia Eagles' famed chief security officer, appeared at Philadelphia Democratic City Committee's fall fundraiser on Monday and promised that the Birds would turn things around after a 2-3 start to the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Dom DiSandro, the Philadelphia Eagles' famed chief security officer, appeared at Philadelphia Democratic City Committee's fall fundraiser on Monday and promised that the Birds would turn things around after a 2-3 start to the 2026 season.

"Big Dom" wears many hats for the Eagles. Alongside his security duties, his job titles also include being the senior advisor to the general manager and gameday coaching operations.

But fixing Philly's offense—which ranks 31st in yards (262.2 YPG), 29th in scoring (18.4 PPG) and has been absolutely dreadful in second halves, contributing to a pair of close losses against the Los Angeles Rams and Jacksonville Jaguars the past two weeks—is beyond even his pay grade.

And given that many of those offensive issues have carried over from the 2025 season, a failure to solve them—and soon—could be the end of the line for head coach Nick Sirianni.

But for now, Big Dom believes the Birds will get back on track.

articles.title: James Cook Could Lose Playing Time amid Fumbling Issues, Bills HC Joe Brady Says
articles.summary: Star running back James Cook fumbled in overtime during Monday night's 37-34 win over the Los Angeles Rams, a gaffe that nearly cost the Buffalo Bills the game.
articles.body:
Star running back James Cook fumbled in overtime during Monday night's 37-34 win over the Los Angeles Rams, a gaffe that nearly cost the Buffalo Bills the game.

In the aftermath, head coach Joe Brady said Cook's usage could be decreased if he doesn't improve his ball security.

"We're putting the ball in harm's way. And we know the way we lose football games is turning the ball over," he told reporters. "Our two best players turned the ball over last night. James has put the ball on the ground. Look, he's doing so many good things running the football. And I don't want to lose sight of how great he's running the football right now. But putting the ball on the ground, it's negating all the positive. I have all the confidence in him, that's why I put him right back out there. But at some point there has to be consequences to when we're putting negative stuff out there. ... That can't happen or it's gonna cost us football games and almost cost us one. We can't confuse that because we won that's OK. It's gotta improve or the carries are gonna decrease."

articles.title: Rams' Alaric Jackson to be suspended by NFL for punching Bills player after MNF loss
articles.summary: This post-game incident has led the NFL to punish the Rams' offensive tackle.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams lost a heartbreaker to the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in Week 5, dropping to 2-3 this year following a blocked field goal in overtime.

But one of the most noteworthy moments from the game happened well afterwards, as Rams offensive tackle Alaric Jackson punched Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb after the game when players were mingling on the field, exchanging jerseys and taking interviews.

The next day, according to Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston , the NFL has punished Jackson for this postgame incident. Jackson has been suspended for two games without pay for punching Chubb.

Rams' Alaric Jackson suspended by NFL for two games after punching Bills' Bradley Chubb

"NFL suspends Rams Alaric Jackson without pay for two games for punching Bills Bradley Chubb, per a league source," Wilson reported Monday afternoon.

This reported suspension should not come as a big surprise after seeing the video from ESPN of what Jackson did after the game.

Jackson walked up to Chubb after the game was well over, and after Chubb said something to Jackson, the Rams' tackle threw a punch at Chubb's head.

Teammates of both players pulled them apart, but for Jackson and the Rams' offensive line, the damage was done.

He's now slated to miss the Week 6 and Week 7 matchups for the Rams, depending on whether an appeal changes his suspension or not.

That means the Rams will be without their starting left tackle for matchups against the Arizona Cardinals and Josh Sweat, and the Las Vegas Raiders and Maxx Crosby in Week 6 and Week 7, respectively.

Taking over for Jackson will be veteran tackle David Quessenberry, who's been in the NFL for a long time and is 36 years old.

While this two-game suspension isn't official, considering how the punch was clearly caught on camera and Jackson's own history, it would not be a surprise if this two-game suspension did come to fruition for Weeks 6 and 7.

articles.title: Jahmyr Gibbs among Alabama football standouts from NFL Week 5
articles.summary: Alabama had another big showing in the NFL during the Week 5 slate, headlined by Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs.
articles.body:
It was another big slate for former Alabama players in the NFL during Week 5, especially on the defensive side of the ball.

For example, four total players in the NFL had multiple interceptions this week. Two of those four were former Alabama players.

Before we get into our weekly list of the top five standouts, two other names worth mentioning are that of Derrick Henry and Germie Bernard. Henry also had a 100-yard rushing day in the Ravens overtime win over the Falcons on Sunday night and Bernard had a career-high 80 receiving yards for the Steelers in their 34-22 win over the Colts.

Here is a look at Alabama's five best performances of NFL Week 5.

Jahmyr Gibbs, Running Back - Detroit Lions

Jahmyr Gibbs remains right in the discussion for the top running back in the league. This week as the Lions blew out the Cardinals, 45-21, Gibbs had a monster day with over 200 yards from scrimmage. He finished up with 25 carries, 151 rushing yards, five catches, 56 receiving yards, and two rushing touchdowns. The 151 rushing yards was the second-most in the league this week. For the season, Gibbs is fourth in the NFL in rushing yards and is tied for the most rushing touchdowns among running backs with Henry.

Will Anderson Jr., Defensive End - Houston Texans

Will Anderson Jr. helped propel the Texans to their first win of the season as they blew out the Titans, 26-3. Anderson finished the game with four tackles and three sacks. The Texans' defense held the Titans to three points and just 187 yards of offense for the game. Anderson was one-of-two players in the NFL this week with three sacks. Anderson now leads the league in sacks for the season with 7.5.

Jordan Battle, Safety - Cincinnati Bengals

Jordan Battle was one of those two former Alabama players with multiple interceptions this week as he hauled in two picks in the Bengals' 31-24 win over the Dolphins. Battle ended up with seven tackles and two interceptions this week. Battle is tied for the league-lead in picks for the season with three.

Xavier McKinney, Safety - Green Bay Packers

McKinney was the other former Tide player with multiple interceptions as the Packers blew out the Bears, 31-7. McKinney had a solo tackle to go along with his two picks. Both of McKinney's interceptions set up Packers' touchdowns on the ensuing drive. McKinney is also of the players tied with Battle for the league-lead in interceptions with three.

Will Reichard, Kicker - Minnesota Vikings

Will Reichard continued his stellar season on Sunday as one of the top kickers in the league. In Sunday's 23-13 Vikings win over the Saints, Reichard once again had a big impact on the Vikings win. He ended up going three-for-three on field goals with two makes from over 50 yards. He finished up with field goals from 55, 54, and 40 yards. Reichard is still perfect on field goals this season at 15-for-15, and has five makes from 50+. Richard is second in the NFL in made field goals this season.
