articles.title: Rams LT Alaric Jackson suspended 2 games for punching Bills player
articles.summary: The Rams will be without LT Alaric Jackson for the next two weeks after he punched Bills OLB Bradley Chubb on Monday night.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams will have to play their next two games without Matthew Stafford's blindside protector. According to Aaron Wilson, the NFL suspended Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson for two games on Tuesday after he punched Buffalo Bills outside linebacker Bradley Chubb during a postgame scuffle Monday night. Michael J. Duarte of The California Post also reported Jackson's suspension.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that the NFL has not yet notified the NFL or the Rams about the suspension, but the expectation is that it'll be for two games.

The incident occurred while players were still on the field after Monday's game. Jackson punched Chubb in the head, knocking his hat off. Chubb then had to be held back by his teammates, ensuring the incident didn't escalate further.

Jackson will miss the Rams' games against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6 and against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7. He will be suspended without pay.

This is the second time Jackson has been suspended in the last three seasons. He was suspended two games to start the 2024 campaign due to a personal conduct violation.

With Jackson missing the next two weeks, the Rams will likely turn to either David Quessenberry or rookie Keagen Trost at left tackle.

articles.title: Alaric Jackson suspended 2 games for punching Bradley Chubb, per report
articles.summary: Rams offensive lineman Alaric Jackson has been suspended for punching Bradley Chubb, per a new report
articles.body:
The NFL has suspended Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Alaric Jackson two games, without pay, for punching Buffalo Bills pass rusher Bradley Chubb following Monday night's game between the two teams, according to a new report from Aaron Wilson .

After a chaotic game saw the Bills defeat the Rams by a final score of 37-34, players from both teams were gathering at midfield for the traditional post-game handshakes and jersey exchanges. Nearby, Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen was conducting an interview. But in the middle of it all a verbal exchange between Jackson and Chubb turned heated, and after Chubb initially walked away from Jackson, the Rams offensive lineman confronted him and then connected with Chubb on a quick right to the jaw that came seemingly out of nowhere.

Jackson had completed the jersey exchange and had a Bills shirt in his hand, as he walked down Chubb and the discussion escalated.

After the incident, Chubb told the California Post that he just "chilled" after the punch:

"It was a close game. And, you know, they always catch the second guy, so I let him swing and my teammates held me back and I just chilled."

The loss on Monday night dropped the Rams to 2-3 on the season. Los Angeles faces the Arizona Cardinals and the Las Vegas Raiders over the next two weeks of the season.

Jackson was suspended for two games by the NFL in 2024 for violating the league's personal conduct policy, following a lawsuit filed by a woman alleging he recorded her without her consent during a sexual encounter. He was also arrested on suspicion of felony domestic violence in June of 2026 and charged with conduct involving a person who "willfully inflicts physical or corporal injury resulting in a 'traumatic condition' on an intimate partner."

Ultimately, criminal charges were not filed and the matter was assigned to a pre-filing diversion program. Jackson was not suspended by the NFL as a result of that decision by the Los Angeles City Attorney's Office.

articles.title: Bengals’ Ja’Marr Chase Gets Good News Amid Tee Higgins Situation
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase got good news that figures to bode well for teammate Tee Higgins. The post Bengals’ Ja’Marr Chase Gets Good Ne...
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals star Ja'Marr Chase did not take the NFL's decision against him lightly.

Chase took action following the multiple fines levied against him and teammate Tee Higgins for what the NFL deemed "obscene gestures" over what the Bengals duo claims is a variation of the "People's Elbow" wrestling move made famous by Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

Regardless of what the true meaning is behind the action, the NFL has decided that its initial ruling against Chase was incorrect.

"Chase's $14,926 fine was successfully appealed as the punishment was overturned by #NFL and #NFLPA appeals officer Derrick Brooks, per a league source," KPRC 2's Aaron Wilson wrote on October 13. "This fine that was overturned stemmed from Chase celebrating a touchdown during a road victory over the #Texans at Reliant Stadium."

The NFL fined Chase twice for the gesture.

While Wilson's report does not explicitly state that the NFL overturned both fines, there is also no reason to believe they would adjudicate the same action differently, especially actions that took place within the same contest.

Tee Higgins Still Waiting as Ja'Marr Chase Gets Good News

Despite the good news for Chase, the Bengals star's co-conspirator in the celebration's situation remains uncertain. That is because it is unknown if Higgins followed Chase's lead following the NFL's initial decision.

"Higgins was fined four times for $59,704 and Chase twice for $29,852," Wilson wrote. "It's unclear if Higgins appealed his fines."

Higgins faces an additional caveat regarding his decision.

Three of his four infractions were the same as Chase's: an "obscene gesture." But his fourth offense was "Illegal celebrations and vulgar acts." It is just as unclear if that is merely a matter of semantics. It stands out amid the consistency of the punishment otherwise.

The Bengals duo was part of a brief stretch that garnered negative attention to the NFL. Many felt the league was overaggressive in penalizing players over their touchdown celebrations.

The league overturned several fines over celebrations they previously deemed violations.

Again, all of that bodes well for Higgins, especially with Chase's verdict being favorable. But it simply is not certain if he took to the requisite steps to benefit from the quick reversal of sentiments from the NFL office.

Bengals Get Best News Possible on Star WR Duo

The fine news is good. However, the Bengals got even better news about Chae and Higgins in their win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 5.

Chase entered the game coming off a week in the concussion protocol after leaving early in Week 4 against the Jacksonville Jaguars . He finished Week 5 with six receptions, 77 yards, and 1 touchdown.

Higgins' (groin) had a quieter day. He hauled in two of his four targets for 22 yards. He still played 69% of the Bengals' offensive snaps .

That is just shy of his average for the 2026 season, per Pro Football Reference.

The Bengals are heading into their bye week. That gives Higgins (and Chase and the rest of the team) some time to heal up. When they return in Week 7, the Bengals will face one of their AFC North rivals, the Baltimore Ravens . That tilt is on the road.

articles.title: NFL expected to suspend Rams LT Alaric Jackson 2 games for postgame punch of Bradley Chubb after 'Monday Night Football'
articles.summary: The incident took place on the field after Buffalo’s 37-34 overtime win at Sofi Stadium in Los Angeles.
articles.body:
The NFL is expected to suspend Los Angeles Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson for two games after he punched Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb in the face in the aftermath of "Monday Night Football," according to multiple reports.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter, the league had not yet notified the Rams or the NFLPA of Jackson's pending suspension as of the time of Tuesday's report.

The incident took place on the field after Buffalo's 37-34 overtime win at Sofi Stadium in Los Angeles on Monday. Jackson was exchanging his jersey with a Bills player when Chubb said something to Jackson and pointed at him from a distance.

Chubb turned around and walked away after his comment. Jackson followed Chubb, and the two exchanged words. Jackson then punched Chubb in the face. ESPN cameras recorded the incident during its postgame coverage.

The suspension leaves the Rams without a key player during a critical juncture of their season.

A Rams team that entered the season as the favorite to win the Super Bowl fell to 2-3 with the loss and will now play its next two games without its most important offensive lineman. Backup David Quessenberry is a candidate to replace Jackson at left tackle, protecting Matthew Stafford's blindside.

The Rams have upcoming games against the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders that Jackson would miss, per the terms of the reported suspension.

Against the Raiders, the Rams would be up against five-time Pro Bowl pass rusher Maxx Crosby. Against the Cardinals, they'll face former Pro Bowler Josh Sweat, who tallied a career-high 12 sacks last season.

articles.title: Dolphins release former first-round pick from practice squad
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins, after five weeks, are swapping out defensive linemen on their practice squad.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins made a pair of moves to their 53-man roster on Tuesday, but they also made two transactions to their practice squad as well, as they released defensive lineman Mazi Smith and signed defensive lineman Jordan Jefferson.

Smith, 25, played at Michigan from 2019-22, earning All-Big Ten honors once before the Dallas Cowboys took him in the first round of the 2023 NFL Draft. After 2.5 years in Dallas, the Jets traded him, and he signed with the Dolphins ' practice squad this September. articles.title: NFL is expected to suspend Rams LT Alaric Jackson two games for postgame punch

articles.body:
The NFL is expected to suspend Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson for two games for a postgame punch Monday night. But Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that the league has yet to notify the team and the NFLPA.

Jackson threw a right hook to Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb after the Rams' 37-34 overtime loss.

Jackson will miss games against the Cardinals and Raiders unless he appeals and wins.

ESPN's cameras caught Jackson exchanging jerseys with Bills defensive lineman Deone Walker at midfield when Chubb appeared to say something to Jackson. Jackson punched Chubb in the face with his right hand before Rams tight end Colby Parkinson pulled Jackson away.

Chubb called it "just emotions" after the game.

Jackson has started all five games this season and missed only one game last season.

articles.title: Saints owner Gayle Benson: I won't accept this level of play as our standard
articles.summary: Seats are starting to heat up in New Orleans.
articles.body:
Seats are starting to heat up in New Orleans.

The Saints lost to the Vikings in Week 5 to fall to 1-4 on the season. The last three losses came in a row and all three came at the Superdome, including a Monday night drubbing at the hands of the Vikings on a night when the Saints celebrated the 20th anniversary of their post-Katrina return to the stadium.

On Tuesday, owner Gayle Benson said that loss "truly disappointed me" during a speech at the Greater New Orleans Quarterback Club Luncheon that left no doubt about how disappointed she is with the team's performance in general. Benson said fans "are right to expect more than we have delivered" through the first five weeks of the season.

"As the owner, the responsibility does start with me," Benson said, via Rod Walker of NOLA.com. "I will not make excuses and I will not accept this level of performance as our standard. I am committed to making the decisions necessary to improving this team. Everyone on this organization understands the urgency. We must prepare better, execute consistently and correct mistakes that are costing us the games."

Benson didn't issue any ultimatums about a more acceptable standard of play, but she did vow to hold people accountable if the Saints are not able to right their ship in the coming weeks.

"Kellen Moore and his coaches are responsible for preparing our players to perform," Benson said. "Mickey Loomis and our football staff are responsible for building a roster capable of sustained success. The players are responsible for their preparation and execution. I am responsible for holding this organization accountable."

Moore is in his second season as the head coach while Loomis has been the General Manager since 2002. The Saints are 7-15 since Moore was hired in 2025 and it sounds like that record will need to get a lot better in order for anyone to feel secure about returning in 2027.

articles.title: Rams' Alaric Jackson Expected to Be Suspended for Punching Bills' Chubb, NFL Rumors Reveal Details
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams are reportedly likely to be without left tackle Alaric Jackson for the next two games.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams are reportedly likely to be without left tackle Alaric Jackson for the next two games.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Tuesday that Jackson is expected to be suspended for two games after he punched Buffalo Bills pass-rusher Bradley Chubb following Monday night's game.

With players gathering on the field after Buffalo's 37-34 victory, there was an altercation that resulted in Jackson throwing a punch and Chubb's teammates restraining him.

The situation even appeared to catch Josh Allen's attention during a postgame interview:

ESPN's Sarah Barshop noted Jackson was exchanging jerseys with Bills defensive lineman Deone Walker when Chubb appeared to say something. The offensive lineman responded by approaching Chubb and punching him.

"Somebody swung, but hey, that's not on me to tell who," Chubb told reporters in the aftermath. "There's cameras out there. I just know, you know what I'm saying, I'm just ready for next week."

He also said, "It was an emotional game. Tempers got flared. But it is what it is. We flushed it and we onto next week."

It was a back-and-forth game, as there were a combined five touchdowns in the fourth quarter alone with Allen and Matthew Stafford exchanging impressive plays and directing drives. It seemed like Buffalo would win when James Cook's touchdown and the ensuing extra point put it up seven with 1:39 remaining, but the Rams responded with a 63-yard touchdown drive of their own to force overtime.

Overtime featured Cook losing a fumble, the Rams' game-winning field-goal attempt being blocked and Tyler Bass connecting on his field goal on the ensuing possession to win it.

For his part, Chubb finished with two tackles when facing Jackson and the rest of the Rams offensive line. Neither defense likely felt great about their efforts on Monday, although the dominant offenses deserve plenty of credit.

The Rams will face the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas for the next two games when Jackson is suspended. Look for David Quessenberry to potentially fill in for the starter until the suspension ends.

articles.title: JIM GRAY: Mike Ditka did it his way. Football will never see another like him
articles.summary: Jim Gray honors Mike Ditka on SiriusXM NFL Radio with Tom Brady, Bill Belichick, Drew Brees and Matthew Stafford remembering America's Coach.
articles.body: America knew him as a football legend. He became the NFL’s symbol of toughness and the emblem of Chicago. Mike Ditka was more than a Hall of Fame player and head coach who led the Bears to their unforgettable Super Bowl XX championship. He was a man who reached well beyond the football field. Coach Ditka was my partner on the radio for a nearly a decade. On our show and podcast this week, "Let’s Go!," broadcast on SiriusXM NFL Radio, I paid tribute to and honored the life of Coach Ditka, along with my fellow co-hosts past and present — Tom Brady, Bill Belichick, Matthew Stafford, Drew Brees and Peter King. They joined me to speak about what Ditka meant to them and to the game of football. Here was our tribute. It's been a very difficult few days since we've learned of the passing of Mike Ditka on Oct. 9, at age 86. Guys like Ditka are very rare. He was a once in a lifetime man. He seemed indestructible. I thought he would beat everything and everyone, and that he just might live forever because a guy like Mike Ditka isn't supposed to die. NFL COACHES SHARE INCREDIBLE MIKE DITKA STORIES AS FOOTBALL WORLD MOURNS THE BEARS LEGEND America's Coach, that's what I called him, and that's who he was. He was my partner on the radio for many, many years. I truly loved him. He was so much fun. He lived his life to the absolute fullest. Tough yet tender. Generous, yet demanding. Funny as hell and a temper that was explosive. He could make you laugh, make you nervous, make you cry, and also feel like the most important person in the room, sometimes all in the same conversation. LIONS HEAD COACH PAYS TRIBUTE TO MIKE DITKA AFTER LEARNING OF HIS DEATH FROM A PRESS CONFERENCE QUESTION He was never polished, never predictable, never interested in being politically correct or being liked by everybody. But perhaps there was no one in sports more beloved by his teammates, by his players, by his colleagues, by his opponents, and even by his critics. MIKE DITKA TRIBUTES POUR IN FROM AROUND THE NFL INCLUDING FANS DRESSING LIKE HIM IN GREEN BAY He was Iron Mike. Da Coach. A man of character, who was, a character. The tombstone of Jackie Robinson reads, "A life is not important, except in the impact it has on other lives." Ditka's impact was enormous on Chicago, the NFL, sports, pop culture, and across the country. I thought he would beat everything and everyone, and that he just might live forever because a guy like Mike Ditka isn't supposed to die. He was bigger than life. Yet, he was always there and available for me personally. He traveled a great distance to introduce me and give the induction the day I was honored with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. His words were heartfelt, helpful, and instructive. "I tell you what an honor this is when you really think about it. I don't know anybody else on this Walk of Fame, but I know you," Ditka said to me and the assembled audience. "What a great honor to be recognized by your peers for your achievements. And I know that you are a professional in everything you do, because when you do it, you do it right. Now I know that there's an art to everything in life. And if there is art to an interview, then you are Michelangelo, believe me, because you are good at that. Now, why is he good? Because he asks tough, hard, fair questions that you've got to answer. And the reason you've got to answer them is because the interview wouldn't work without your answer. And that's what makes him so good. I'm really proud to be your friend. We've been together for a long time," Ditka continued. "Let me tell you something that I know for a fact about life. If you have no critics, you have no successes. God bless you." That sentiment, is so enlightening and edifying to anyone in public life. He knew it, and he chose successes. Critics be damned. Ditka truly had it all. The mustache, cigar, volatility, the winning, the loyalty. He was one of a kind. And for the people who knew him beyond the public persona, there was another side. The one of extraordinary kindness. They saw the moments when the bluster disappeared. Mike Ditka helped, truly helped, so many people. Whether they were fellow players in need, youngsters in crisis, seniors in peril, families that were struggling, or strangers in distress. Ditka was the most generous person I've ever known. I saw his commitment to contribute, respond, and was constantly giving of his time and resources. And he wanted and expected absolutely nothing in return for his countless, truly endless acts of goodwill. That's the part you can't put in a highlight reel, and maybe that's the part that matters most. His life was lived to the lyrics of the song, "My Way." "For what is a man? What has he got? If not himself, then he has not. To say the things he truly feels, and not the words of one who kneels. The record shows I took the blows and did it my way." When somebody like that is gone, you don't just miss what he did. You miss his presence. There will never be another Mike Ditka because as Ralph Waldo Emerson once wrote, "When nature removes a great man, people explore the horizon for a successor; but none comes, and none will. His class is extinguished with him." Mike Ditka, my dear friend, America's coach, an institution and national treasure, was in a class all his own. Every time we ended a conversation, Mike would never say goodbye. His words would always be, "God bless, Jimmy." So, I won't say goodbye to Coach Ditka. I will follow his lead. God bless, Coach. May God rest your soul and bless your family. *** Here is what the all-time greats had to say during the show about Coach Ditka. This week’s episode of "Let’s Go!" can be heard here. Tom Brady, 7 time Super Bowl winning quarterback: "There are so many things I loved about Coach Ditka from watching from afar and getting to know him over the course of my NFL career. He was as tough as the city that he coached in and he was the first tight end ever in the Hall of Fame. I heard Gronk on the pregame show say he owed a lot to Coach Ditka. Without Coach Ditka, there are no players like Rob Gronkowski who revolutionized the tight end position. And without Rob Gronkowski, I'm down a bunch of Super Bowls. So I gotta thank Coach Ditka for a lot of reasons. He won a Super Bowl as a player, he won a Super Bowl as a head coach. And as a quarterback, I always know what a great tight end means to an offense. He is my safety valve. That's your third down answer. And every one I ever threw to owes something to Mike." Tom Brady: "On TV, he also revolutionized the game with his media career. He never softened on a word. There was never a filter. There was no fluff. It was just all football. Rest easy, Coach Ditka." Bill Belichick, 6 time Super Bowl winning head coach: "As a player, Mike was extremely tough, competitive, all business, a guy you certainly didn't wanna mess with and he set the tone for the teams that he played on. It was similar as a coach. He had that same toughness that transferred to his team and, and players. And you knew anytime you went up against him, like you were going to be in an absolute brawl and fight all the way to the finish because that's the way he and his teams competed. Loved Mike. Loved Mike and what he meant to the game. And we'll miss him." Matthew Stafford, NFL MVP Los Angeles Rams quarterback: "I had the pleasure of being on some of the NFL shows with him. You know, his presence was really something else. All these guys, they play football, they coach football, then they move to talking about football and they become just a guy that talks about football. But Ditka was always coach, right? I mean, and I remember, getting to do those shows with him. He had the cigar unlit under the table. He was just true to himself and that was such a cool thing to be a part of." CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION Drew Brees, Hall of Fame, Super Bowl-winning quarterback: "He was not only an incredible player, but an incredible coach. There's a type of leadership where you just see things happen before they happen. You just have a vision for what the way that things should be, and then your contributions to getting it to that point. It's a rare trait. I think Mike was no question, was certainly one of those guys and man, he's gonna be missed." Peter King, Award-winning NFL sportswriter: "Nothing ever about Mike Ditka was invented, was put on anything. He always was himself. Ditka, as a player, as a coach, as a broadcaster, was authentic and he was perfect and he was dedicated to be great at whatever he did at that moment." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

articles.title: Brian Flores' lawyer says memo to Raiders before team's coaching search portrayed client as 'angry Black man'

articles.body: The lawyers for Brian Flores say a recruiting memo used by the Las Vegas Raiders while considering the Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator for their head-coaching job is evidence that teams are retaliating against him for filing a racial discrimination lawsuit and that discriminatory hiring practices remain in place across the NFL. The document that the NFL and search firm Korn Ferry hoped would remain sealed became public Tuesday after the magistrate judge overseeing the discovery process in Flores's class-action lawsuit previously rejected Korn Ferry's arguments to keep the document confidential. The Korn Ferry document, as first reported by Front Office Sports, presents two columns under the heading, "Brian Flores -- Strengths and Weaknesses" SUPREME COURT HANDS NFL A LOSS IN BRIAN FLORES DISCRIMINATION LAWSUIT Among the Flores weaknesses, per Korn Ferry: Flores attorney Michael Willemin told FOS some of these descriptions conjure the image of an "angry Black man." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Even one of the six positive points that Korn Ferry credits to Flores can be questionable in a discrimination suit because it paints Flores as someone who learned to speak and present himself positively because he got to meet rich White people despite being reared in a tough predominantly Black and Hispanic neighborhood. The law firms representing Flores, Wigdor LLP and Elefterakis, Elefterakis & Panek, issued a statement on Tuesday about the Korn Ferry memo: "The recently unsealed documents demonstrate two unfortunate, but unsurprising, realities," the statement reads. "First, that Mr. Flores’ decision to hold the league and its teams accountable for systemic race discrimination has been met with unlawful retaliation. "Second, discrimination continues to play a significant role in the hiring process for NFL Head Coaches, as evidenced by the fact that the candidate profile prepared for the Raiders leans heavily on racial stereotypes. We and Mr. Flores are committed to eradicating the institutional racism and retaliation that permeates the league, its teams and their partners." The memo in question was prepared by Korn Ferry for the Las Vegas Raiders before the team's most recent coaching search that ultimately resulted in Klint Kubiak being hired. Flores was not interviewed by the Raiders. Flores, who is Black, sued the NFL and its 32 teams in February 2022, specifically naming the Miami Dolphins, Denver Broncos and New York Giants. Flores, who coached the Dolphins from February 2019 to January 2022, alleges in his suit that the Dolphins defamed him. If the Korn Ferry reference to Flores being "the worst hiring decision we've ever made" is shown to be from a Dolphins executive, that could be used to prove the defamation claim. articles.body:
The fallout from the Los Angeles Rams' defeat by the Buffalo Bills rumbled on as offensive lineman Alaric Jackson was suspended for punching an opponent while kicker Harrison Mevis has been released.

Jackson was handed a two-game ban by the NFL after he struck Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb following Monday's 37-34 overtime loss.

Chubb was talking to players from both teams near midfield when Jackson approached him and punched him in the jaw.

"It's just emotions, you know what I mean? Emotional game, it was a close game," Chubb said.

Jackson is now set to miss the Rams' next two games against the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders.

Meanwhile, the Rams have decided to cut Mevis and sign fellow kicker Blake Grupe from the New York Jets' practice squad.

Mevis missed a field goal in regulation and had another attempt blocked in overtime against the Bills, which Rams head coach Sean McVay said "cost us the game".

"The kicking game, especially with our PAT, field goal, not even close to good enough," McVay said.

Mevis, 24, has made five of his past nine field goal attempts, including only one of his last four across the past two games.

Grupe, 27, has converted 81.9% of his field goals and 98% of his extra-point attempts in 50 NFL games with the New Orleans Saints and Indianapolis Colts.

articles.title: NFL legend Terry Bradshaw says he realizes his TV career is ‘coming to an end’
articles.summary: Pro Football Hall of Famer and Fox broadcaster Terry Bradshaw told NBC News on Tuesday his television career ‘is coming to an end.’
articles.body: Pro Football Hall of Famer and Fox broadcaster Terry Bradshaw told NBC News on Tuesday his television career is winding down. “I realize my time on television as a sports broadcaster is coming to an end,” Bradshaw, 78, said on “NBC News Daily” while discussing his new memoir, “Looking for Terry.” Bradshaw was asked about his busy schedule when he made the remark, noting that in addition to his writing, he has a horse ranch, a bourbon line and several grandchildren. “I just love life. Billy Graham said, and I never forgot this quote, he said, ‘The day you retire is the day you start dying,’” Bradshaw said. He added: “I’m a workaholic, I love to work,” before saying he knew he was nearing the end of his broadcasting career. Bradshaw first began his career as an analyst in 1984, the same year he retired. He was a color commentator for CBS until he joined the network’s pregame show in 1990. In 1994, Bradshaw joined Fox, and has appeared on their Sunday pregame show ever since. Him and Howie Long are the only two members of the show who have been on the “Fox NFL Sunday” desk since its inception. A Louisiana native, Bradshaw spent the entirety of his storied playing career with the Pittsburgh Steelers, quarterbacking the legendary franchise from 1970 through 1983. He played in only one game his final season, retiring due to elbow troubles. Bradshaw led the Steelers to four Super Bowl wins between 1974 and 1979, becoming the first quarterback in NFL history to win three (as well as four) Super Bowls. He was named Super Bowl MVP twice, and also won a regular season MVP in 1978. Bradshaw was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1989, and no Pittsburgh player has worn his iconic No. 12 since his retirement. In addition to his broadcasting career, Bradshaw has spent part of his post-playing days as an actor. He appeared in television shows as such as the sitcom “Everybody Loves Raymond,” the fantasy football comedy “The League,” and even participated in “The Masked Singer.” In 2006, Bradshaw played the father of Matthew McConnaughey’s character in the romantic comedy “Failure to Launch,” appearing nude in one scene. In his memoir, Bradshaw also discusses some of the personal issues he’s faced in retirement, including battling cancer and depression. “I couldn’t understand why I had this horrible sinking feeling, and I was so miserable,” Bradshaw said of dealing with depression. Bradshaw added that it was difficult as a former NFL player to open up about his mental health issues, saying that a good friend of his even once made fun of him for discussing his depression in the past. “It was a hard thing for me to decide to do, because I didn’t want it to be taken lightly, and I didn’t want to be laughed at,” Bradshaw said. He added: “A lot of men think if they dealt with depression that people are going to see it as a weakness. It’s a disease. It’s a disconnect.”

A recently unsealed recruiting firm's report on Brian Flores has multiple examples of "racial stereotypes" and amounts to unlawful retaliation for the coach's discrimination lawsuit against the NFL, according to his lawyers.

"The recently unsealed documents demonstrate two unfortunate, but unsurprising, realities," attorney Michael J. Willemin wrote in a statement. Second, discrimination continues to play a significant role in the hiring process for NFL Head Coaches, as evidenced by the fact that the candidate profile prepared for the Raiders leans heavily on racial stereotypes. We and Mr. Flores are committed to eradicating the institutional racism and retaliation that permeates the league, its teams and their partners."

The NFL didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

One of the strengths listed says Flores is a "polished and a good presenter despite growing up in Brownsville, Brooklyn (same as Mike Tyson). He was able to build a strong friendship with a billionaire's son which gave him opportunities to socialize and learn how to build relationships with white-collar and upper-class individuals."

Brownsville is a predominately Black and Hispanic neighborhood in Brooklyn.

Other negatives listed included that Flores' "personality is unpredictable" and that he "once threatened violence to his GM and made irrational demands during an ownership meeting."

The report goes on to say that a long-term senior executive said Flores "may have changed since, but he was the worst hiring decision we've ever made."

The final negative was that the ongoing litigation related to the coach's discrimination case against the NFL could cause a distraction.

Flores, who is Black, sued the league and three teams in February 2022, alleging the league was "rife with racism" regarding its hiring practices when it comes to Black coaches. Flores had recently been fired from his head coaching job with the Miami Dolphins.

Big Dom Vows Eagles Will 'Get this Fixed'

articles.body: We're through the first five weeks of the NFL season, and I'm here to report that Cooper DeJean and Abby Summers continue to choose love over divisional rivalry. It's a beautiful thing to witness. Forget any forced narratives being pushed by the league. The relationship between the Philadelphia Eagles defensive back and the Dallas Cowboys cheerleader should be getting a lot more attention. This is a romance that's defying all odds in the NFC East. These two are making it work despite being members of opposing franchises. Week 5 of the long season showed their commitment. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. By Sunday, she had traded in her pom-poms and the iconic Cowboys cheerleader outfit for Eagles green as Philadelphia lost in unbelievable fashion to the Jacksonville Jaguars across the pond in London. COWBOYS HIRE LONGTIME NFL COACH OUT OF RETIREMENT TO ADDRESS TEAM'S BRUTAL DEFENSIVE START Now don't go around pointing fingers at Abby Summers as if she's responsible for the Eagles loss. That's not fair. They had that game in the bag until the crazy kickoff decision at the end. That's not her fault. As far as any of us know, mostly because she wasn't one of the WAGs who popped in the NFL's propaganda campaign, she wasn’t keeping Cooper DeJean out of the film room during training camp for social media videos. How each of them bounces back after tough losses will tell a lot about what the season has in store for them. In a couple of weeks, we'll know even more. That's because the Cowboys and Eagles will play each other for the first time this season, and it will be on Monday Night Football in Philadelphia. Doing it at Lincoln Financial Field as a Dallas Cowboys cheerleader is something completely different. If Cooper DeJean and Abby Summers can make it through that, they can make it through anything. Including a game on Thanksgiving in Dallas. I'm not rooting for either team, but I will continue to root for the rival couple.

articles.title: Nets' Julius Randle discusses joining team via trade this offseason
articles.summary: Brooklyn Nets forward Julius Randle came to the Nets this offseason via trade from the Minnesota Timberwolves and he discussed his thought process.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- Brooklyn Nets forward Julius Randle coming to the Nets in a trade from the Minnesota Timberwolves this offseason was one of the more surprising moves that happened throughout the NBA. Brooklyn has been looking to add talent to the roster following a 2025-26 season where they finished with a 20-62 record and regardless of how it happened, Randle is feeling good about being with the Nets.

"It's a business and things happen. But, when you're somewhere where you're really wanted, and you have that validation with an organization really appreciating you and what you bring to the table, it's an incredible feeling," Randle said, per Brian Lewis of the New York Post. In the early days of the offseason, Randle was traded to the Nets along with the No. 28 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft (forward Joshua Jefferson) in exchange for just the No. 33 overall pick.

"It just drops the anxiety and the worry or the pressure. You feel like you can be your best self. So, from Day 1, I felt that: the support. I damn near get goose bumps just thinking about it because the support has been amazing," Randle continued, per Lewis. Given what the Timberwolves received from Brooklyn in the deal , Randle was seen as a salary-dump in the move, but it seems like that hasn't affected how he feels about his current team. Veterans, both players and coaches, around the league understand Randle's value on and off the court.

"Julius Randle had some great seasons in Minnesota, we'll see how that translates here. But, he played really good for the T-Wolves," Philadelphia 76ers head coach Nick Nurse said of Randle prior to the Nets beating the 76ers 114-108 in their preseason matchup last week. "[He's] a tough in-and-out cover, right? Perimeter shooting improved off the bounces. Always really good. His back to the basket's always really good. So, it kind of gives them another veteran type go-to guy."

Through Brooklyn's three preseason games, Randle is averaging 13.7 points, 4.0 rebounds, and 4.7 assists per game while shooting 50.0% from the field and 50.0% from behind the three-point line in 21.0 minutes played per night. Randle will likely be the starter at power forward next to small forward Michael Porter Jr. and based off the former Kentucky Wildcat's comments, it seems like he's ready to do what it takes to win in Brooklyn.

articles.title: Micah Parsons says Jayden Daniels 'probably cost' Dan Quinn his Commanders head coach job after Week 5 tie
articles.summary: Micah Parsons claimed Jayden Daniels' overtime sack against the New York Giants probably cost Dan Quinn his Washington Commanders coaching job.
articles.body: Jayden Daniels taking a sack instead of throwing the ball out of bounds cost the Washington Commanders a much-needed overtime victory against the New York Giants on Sunday. Green Bay Packers star defensive end Micah Parsons believes that action, which led to a 27-27 tie in Week 5, cost Daniels’ head coach his job. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn’s seat has been hot for some time, but it may be at a scorching level now after what occurred in Week 5 when Daniels went down in field goal range without a timeout and the clock hit zero in overtime to force a tie. The Commanders were left stunned, as Quinn threw down his headset on the sideline knowing that his team should be 2-3 instead of 1-3-1. And frankly, he had to know the questions and speculations about his job security would be even louder. Parsons added to it during the latest episode of "The Edge with Micah Parsons," where he placed blame on Daniels in that final moment. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "Jayden Daniels probably cost my man Dan Quinn his job, to be honest with you," Parsons said in the episode. "I’m a big Jayden Daniels fan, but, the reality is he probably cost a lot of people their jobs this past weekend." Quinn was Parsons’ defensive coordinator with the Dallas Cowboys from 2021-23 before accepting the head coaching post with the Commanders. The Commanders had blown a lead they held most of the game at home on Sunday, with Malik Nabers tying it up with a touchdown in the fourth quarter to force overtime. And Giants kicker Dominic Zvada, who missed three field goals in the contest, missed a 46-yard attempt on the opening overtime drive. Daniels should’ve just thrown the ball away, but debate over the final play in overtime has brought up the coaching staff and the team as a whole deserving blame – not just the signal-caller. MAGIC JOHNSON MAKES RARE CRITICAL POST AFTER COMMANDERS' HEAD-SCRATCHING TIE AGAINST GIANTS "All respectfully, we get coached so much on these situations that I'm a defensive player and this is programmed to me," Parsons added. "I know what to do in those situations. "There’s no way I’m taking a sack with 14 seconds left and no timeouts. And mind you, it’d be different if Jayden Daniels was a rookie. This is your third year. You’ve been to the NFC Championship Game, you’ve been in big moments before. To me, even after the sack, you’re casually getting up. … I’m like, ‘You just took a sack.’ … He’s not even urgently getting up." Either way, after a brutal 2025 season that didn’t build upon reaching the NFC Championship Game in 2024, it hasn’t been great for Quinn and the Commanders to begin 2026. They sit at the bottom of a topsy-turvy NFC East division, and could’ve certainly used the victory to move to 2-3 just like the Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles. For Daniels, it was a learning moment, but one Parsons and others believe he should’ve known about before even snapping the ball. It was his first game back since dislocating his left elbow again in Week 2 against the Cowboys on the road. Daniels did, however, play a solid game, especially with his legs. The injury didn’t seem to make him hesitant to run, as he rushed for 103 yards with two touchdowns on the ground, while going 17-of-25 through the air for 199 yards. There’s no doubting the talent the former Heisman Trophy winner has – it’s been on full display since winning the 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year. And though his teammates were also lackadaisical when Daniels was sacked, the fact the quarterback went down with the ball in his hands with no timeouts in the first place is a real issue that Parsons believes trumps any other argument. Will it cost Quinn his job? Leadership comes into question when the quarterback pulls that sort of stunt. Quinn said after the game that the blame "does not fall on" Daniels. However, Commanders left guard Chris Paul told 7News DC that the lack of timeouts was discussed in the huddle before the snap. It starts with everybody, top down. Ultimately, it’s on me." Though he said it was on him, Parsons wanted more accountability. "I’m a player. I’m a big JD5 fan, but that’s inexcusable bro. The lack of urgency, that’s something … I would’ve had to say something in the locker room. I would’ve had to come talk to him, like, ‘Yo, that’s not OK.’" SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER
